data.title:
A Nitrogen-specific Interactome Analysis Sheds Light on the Role of the SnRK1 and TOR Kinases in
Plant Nitrogen Signaling part1 AP-MS and TurboID
data.projectDescription: Nitrogen (N) is of utmost importance for plant growth and development. Multiple studies have shown that N signaling is tightly coupled with carbon (C) levels, but the interplay between C/N metabolism and growth remains largely an enigma. Nonetheless, the protein kinases sucrose non-fermenting 1 (SNF1)-related kinase 1 (SnRK1) and target of rapamycin (TOR), two ancient central metabolic regulators, are emerging as key integrators that link C/N status with growth. Despite their pivotal importance, the exact mechanisms behind the sensing of N status and its integration with C availability to drive metabolic decisions are largely unknown. Especially for SnRK1 it is not clear how this kinase responds to altered N levels. Therefore, we first monitored N-dependent SnRK1 kinase activity at high resolution with our in vivo separation of phase-based activity reporter of kinase (SPARK), revealing a contrasting N-dependency in shoot and root tissues. Next, using affinity purification (AP) and proximity labeling (PL) coupled to mass spectrometry (MS) experiments, we constructed an N-specific SnRK1 and TOR interactome in Arabidopsis thaliana cell cultures during N-starved and  repleted growth conditions. To broaden our understanding of the N-dependency of the TOR/SnRK1 signaling pathway, the resulting network was compared to corresponding C-related networks, identifying a large number of novel, N-specific interactors. Moreover, through integration of N dependent transcriptome and phosphoproteome data, we were able to pinpoint additional N dependent network components, revealing SnRK1 regulatory proteins that might function at the crosstalk of C/N signaling. Finally, confirmation of known and identification of novel interactors, such as IRE1A and RAB18, indicate that the endoplasmic reticulum functions as a key regulatory hub for TOR and SnRK1 via integration of C/N signaling.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Arabidopsis Cell Culture Transformation and Biomass Generation for Interactomics All GSrhino and linkerTurboID-3xHA fusion constructs were transferred to A. tumefaciens C58C1 RifR (pMP90), transformed into the dark-growing Arabidopsis PSB-D cell culture and upscaled in standard nutrient-rich conditions. Three days after subculturing, cells were washed and resuspended in N-free medium containing 0.5 % (w/v) sucrose. After 48 h of N starvation, cultures were split into two shake flasks, and 1 mM KNO3 was added to one while the other served as N-starvation control. For the TurboID cultures, 50 uM biotin was added 48 h after N starvation, and cells were grown further for 15 min or 1 h with or without KNO3. Cells were harvested through vacuum infiltration, sampling 7,5 gram of PSB-D cells for triplicate AP-MS experiments, or 9 grams of PSB-D cells for triplicate PL-MS experiments, and harvested cell material was frozen in N2 and stored at -70°C. Isolation of Protein Complexes by GSrhino-Based Affinity Purification GSrhino-based affinity purification (AP) experiments were performed in triplicate starting from 2.5 g of frozen cell material per replicate (Van Leene et al., 2019). Briefly, protein complexes were trapped through the Protein G part of the GSrhino tag by incubating 25 mg total protein extract per replicate for 45 min with 50 uL in-house prepared magnetic immunoglobulin G (IgG) bead suspension. Beads were washed three times with 500 uL extraction buffer, once with 500 uL extraction buffer without detergent, and once with 800 uL 50 mM NH4HCO3 (pH 8.0). The wash buffer was removed and beads were incubated in 50 uL 50 mM NH4HCO3 supplemented with 1 g Trypsin/Lys-C (Promega) for 4 h at 37°C. Next, the digest was separated from the beads and further incubated overnight with 0.5 g Trypsin/Lys-C at 37°C. Finally, the digest was centrifuged at 20,800 rcf for 5 min, and supernatant was dried in a SpeedVac and stored at 20°C until MS analysis.  TurboID-Based Proximity Labeling (PL) Proximity labeling experiments were performed from 3g harvested cell material per replicate, as described in detail for Arabidopsis PSB-D cells (Arora et al., 2020), using denaturing extraction buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 2% (w/v) SDS, 8 M urea) and with the additional acid elution step following the Trypsin/Lys-C digest, as described in (Van Leene et al., 2022).  LC-MS/MS Analysis On-bead digested samples were analyzed on a Q Exactive (ThermoFisher Scientific) using standard procedures. Briefly, peptides were redissolved in loading solvent A (0.1% TFA in water/ACN (98:2, v/v)) and injected for LC-MS/MS analysis on an Ultimate 3000 RSLC nano LC (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) in-line connected to a Q Exactive mass spectrometer. The peptides were first loaded on a trapping column (made in-house, 100um internal diameter (I.D.) × 20 mm, 5um beads C18 Reprosil-HD, Dr. Maisch, Ammerbuch-Entringen, Germany), and after flushing from the trapping column, the peptides were separated on a 50cm µPAC™ column with C18-endcapped functionality (Pharmafluidics, Belgium) kept at a constant temperature of 50°C. Peptides were eluted by a nonlinear gradient from 99% solvent A' (0.1% formic acid in water) ) to 10% solvent B′ (0.1% formic acid in water/ACN, 20/80 (v/v)) in 9 min, 30% solvent B’ in 29 min, 50% solvent B’ in 34 min at a flow rate of 300 nL/min, followed by a 5 min wash reaching 95% solvent B’. The mass spectrometer was operated in data-dependent, positive ionization mode, automatically switching between MS and MS/MS acquisition for the five most abundant peaks in a given MS spectrum.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: From Thermo raw files, MGF files were created using Mascot Distiller (versions 2.5.0.0 and 2.8.2.0, Matrix Science). A peak list was only generated when the MS/MS spectrum contained more than 10 peaks. There was no de-isotoping and the relative S/N limit was set to 2. Homology-based protein identification was done using Mascot (versions 2.6.2 and 2.8.2, Matrix Science) with database Araport11plus. Variable modifications were set to oxidation(M), acetyl(protein N-termini), and for PL experiments, also biotin(K). Mass tolerance on MS was set to 10 ppm (with Mascot’s C13 option set to 1) and the MS/MS tolerance at 20 mmu. The peptide charge was set to 2+, 3+ and 4+ and the instrument to ESI-QUAD. Trypsin was set as protease, allowing for 2 missed cleavages, and cleavage when R or K is followed by P. Only high-confident peptides, ranked 1 and with scores above the threshold score, set at 99% confidence, were withheld. Proteins with at least 1 unique peptide were initially retained. The Thermo raw files were also searched with MaxQuant (versions 1.6.10.43 and 2.2.0.0) against the Araport11plus database. For AP-MS, variable modifications were set to oxidation(M), acetyl(protein N-termini), and phospho(S,T,Y). For PL-MS, variable modifications were set to oxidation(M), acetyl(protein N-termini), phospho(S,T) and biotin(K). Mass tolerance on precursor ions was set to 4.5 ppm and on fragment ions to 20 ppm. Trypsin was set as protease, allowing for 2 missed cleavages, and cleavage when R or K was followed by P. PSM and protein identifications were filtered using a target-decoy approach at false discovery rate (FDR) of 1%. Proteins identified with at least 1 unique peptide were retained. To determine bait-specific interactors in the AP-MS data, for all identifications, normalized spectral abundance factors (NSAF) in the 3 replicates were compared to the NSAFs in a large in-house dataset consisting of 515 AP-MS experiments on 109 bait proteins, not related to SnRK1 or TOR signaling and grouped functionally into 28 bait-groups. Thereto, the ratio of the average bait and control NSAF values were determined as a measure of fold enrichment, and a two-tailed Student’s t-test was performed comparing bait and control Ln-transformed NSAF values to determine the enrichment significance. t-test p-values were -Log10 transformed and infinite values were replaced by a constant -Log10 p-value of 325. Identifications were considered significantly enriched if they passed 1 of the following criteria: i) 2-peptide identifications present in at least 2 out of 3 replicates and present in less than 3 bait-groups in the large AP-MS dataset, with a mean NSAF ratio >= 10 AND a  -Log10(p-value) >= 10, or with a mean NSAF ratio >= 20 AND a -Log10(p-value) >= 8, ii) 1-peptide identifications present in 3 replicates, present in the large dataset with less than 5 bait-groups, and with a mean NSAF ratio >= 10 AND a  -Log10(p-value) >= 10. As a 2nd filter, average NSAF values were compared to the average NSAF value over 6 PSB-D WT control experiments, harvested 3x under N-starvation and 3x under KNO3-repletion conditions. Proteins were retained as specific if their Affinity Enrichment Score (AES), i.e. the product of their NSAF ratio and -Log10(p-value), was >= 100. To determine specific proteins in the PL-MS data, a similar approach was used, integrating a large in-house PL-MS dataset derived from 283 PL-MS experiments covering 37 bait proteins not related to SnRK1 or TOR signaling. For the 1st filter, NSAF ratios, -Log10(p-values) and AES were calculated for all identified proteins. Proteins with an AES >= 20 were retained. A 2nd filtering was implemented to correct for proteome changes provoked by the N-starvation/KNO3-repletion condition. Hereto, all bait experiments were analyzed by MaxQuant LFQ analysis, together with their corresponding negative controls (WT or GFP-TurboID) harvested under similar conditions. The MaxQuant proteingroup.txt files were uploaded into Perseus (version 1.6.15.0) and analyzed as described before (Van Leene et al., 2019; Van Leene et al., 2022). Triplicate bait and negative control experiments were separately grouped and compared through Volcano plot analysis (FDR=0.01, S0=1) to detect specific interactors for each PL-MS experiment. Finally, this MaxQuant LFQ analysis was integrated with the NSAF dataset of the 1st filtering, retaining only filtered proteins from the NSAF dataset that were at least once significantly differing in the MaxQuant LFQ analysis with a bait of the same complex (SnRK1 or TOR). Proteins identified by only 1 unique peptide were retained if the protein was identified in all 3 repeats, or if the protein was identified with 1 unique peptide in at least 2 replicates and additionally found with at least 2 peptides in another PL-MS experiment with a bait of the same complex.
